rationale: This is a soft-gate restatement of the archive's AccrualsOfBarelyProfitableFirms rather than a new mechanism, and the stated justification is internally shaky — SIGN(pi) is a two-valued variable whose rank contributes a step, not a "graded tilt with no mass point," so the design merely rescales the already-tested asymmetry gate.

Averaging the ranks of |pi|/lt and |pi|/at blends two near-identical archive gates whose cross-sectional ranks are almost surely highly correlated, so the outcome will interpolate between two known results and teach nothing about mechanism — this is the definition of a cosmetic variant.

Testing persistence rather than a one-year snapshot of breakeven proximity is a defensible new dimension given the archive's evidence that multi-year states dominate, though the construct is partly confounded because |MA(pi,3)| is also small for firms whose large profits and large losses cancel, mixing "chronically marginal" with "volatile."

A rank-average union of two gates that have each already been tested individually is a portfolio blend whose result will predictably land between the two parents, and the "union broadens the population" argument does not survive the fact that the multiplicative gates are rank-based tilts, not hard intersections that zero out mass.

This is the only proposal that changes the accrual leg rather than the gate, and within-firm demeaning is a genuinely different construct (effectively working-capital acceleration) that isolates a design question the archive has never tested; the one caveat is that a contemporaneous three-year MA both demeans and mechanically shrinks the current build, so a null result would be ambiguous between "firm norm irrelevant" and "signal attenuated."

Replacing Δlt with Δ(dltt+dlc) removes a real accounting overlap with the payables term inside the accrual leg, so this is a substantive rather than decorative fix, but it remains a hybrid of two existing archive signals and the incremental information content over AccrualsWhileBorrowingExceedsEarnings is likely modest.
